name: Tekoa
overview: Tekoa is a male figure from the tribe of Judah, identified specifically as the son of Ashhur. The biblical record of Tekoa is brief, with no additional notes or detailed narrative provided. His mention situates him within the genealogical framework of Judah's descendants.
namesAndTitles: Tekoa is recorded as a proper name in Scripture, with no specific meaning or divine origin indicated. The name is simply presented as it appears in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Tekoa is noted as the son of Ashhur, establishing a clear father-son relationship within the tribe of Judah. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide further family details or relationships for Tekoa.
scriptureSignificance: Tekoa's significance lies primarily in his genealogical placement within the tribe of Judah, as the son of Ashhur. Although the biblical text does not elaborate on his personal deeds or role, his inclusion in the lineage underscores the careful preservation of Israel's tribal heritage. Such genealogical records contribute to the broader biblical narrative of God's covenant people.
